title: Kobalos Linux Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate a high confidence MISP event about a complex Linux backdoor named Kobalos, targeting high performance computing infrastructure.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The scenario is based on a high confidence MISP event about a complex Linux backdoor named Kobalos, targeting high performance computing infrastructure. The malware is known to be portable to Linux, BSD, Solaris, and possibly AIX and Windows. It communicates with its Command and Control (C2) server over SSH on port 7070 using the IP address 151.80.57.191.

levels.title: Access
levels.cloud_content: Connect to the sandbox using SSH as user cyrano with password cyrano.
levels.local_content: Set up your local environment for accessing the sandbox.

levels.title: Identify/investigate/detect suspicious service
levels.content: Determine if the sshd service is running on the target host.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Use the ss command to list open network connections and services.

levels.title: Identify/investigate/detect persistence mechanism
levels.content: Investigate how Kobalos establishes persistence on the target host.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Look for signs of the malware embedded in OpenSSH server executable (sshd) or stand-alone variants that connect to a C&C server or wait for an inbound connection on a given TCP port.

levels.title: Identify/investigate/detect malicious services
levels.content: Determine if there are any other suspicious services running on the target host that could be related to Kobalos.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Use netstat or ss commands to list open network connections and services.
